nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Scientific notation
nodes.summary: Scientific notation Calculate with powers of ten and report a normalized coeﬀicient.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Arithmetic patterns
nodes.summary: Arithmetic patterns Recover terms and differences; evaluate finite sums and sigma expressions; interpret approximate additive models.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Geometric patterns
nodes.summary: Geometric patterns Connect a first term and ratio to later terms, finite sums, sigma expressions and multiplicative models.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Growth of money and depreciation
nodes.summary: Growth of money and depreciation Use compounding periods, percentage losses and inflation to calculate nominal and real values.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Integer powers and logarithm notation
nodes.summary: Integer powers and logarithm notation Simplify integer powers and interpret base-10 and natural logarithms.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Direct algebraic reasoning
nodes.summary: Direct algebraic reasoning Use exact numerical and algebraic deduction; distinguish equality from iden- tity and check transformations.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Rational powers and logarithmic equations
nodes.summary: Rational powers and logarithmic equations Use roots, logarithm laws and change of base; solve exponential equations with valid domains.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Infinite geometric sums
nodes.summary: Infinite geometric sums Recognize convergence, evaluate an infinite sum and combine related geomet- ric series.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Binomial coeﬀicients
nodes.summary: Binomial coeﬀicients Use Pascal coeﬀicients and combinations to extract terms from positive-integer powers.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Counting and generalized expansions
nodes.summary: Counting and generalized expansions Count ordered and unordered selections with restrictions; expand rational powers with in a valid interval.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Partial fractions
nodes.summary: Partial fractions Separate proper rational expressions over two distinct linear factors and use the decomposition.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Cartesian complex numbers
nodes.summary: Cartesian complex numbers Calculate with i, conjugates and Cartesian components; interpret modulus and argument on an Argand plane.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Polar and exponential complex forms
nodes.summary: Polar and exponential complex forms Convert representations; connect multiplication and division to changes in scale and angle.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Complex powers and polynomial roots
nodes.summary: Complex powers and polynomial roots Use conjugate pairs and de Moivre powers; extend to rational exponents and find every complex root.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Induction, contradiction and counterexamples
nodes.summary: Induction, contradiction and counterexamples Use induction with a base case and inductive step, contradiction reasoning and counterexamples to universal claims.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Linear systems
nodes.summary: Linear systems Solve up to three equations; distinguish a unique solution, a solution family and inconsistency.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Straight lines
nodes.summary: Straight lines Convert line equations; calculate slopes and intercepts; use parallel and per- pendicular directions.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: F unction language
nodes.summary: F unction language Identify inputs, outputs, domain and range; interpret a function as a model and its inverse as a reversed mapping.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Reading and representing graphs
nodes.summary: Reading and representing graphs Connect equations, tables and graph shapes; interpret graphs of sums and differences; select appropriate graph windows.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Graph features and intersections
nodes.summary: Graph features and intersections Locate zeros, vertices, extrema, symmetry, intercepts and asymptotes; find intersections numerically.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Composition and inversion
nodes.summary: Composition and inversion Apply functions in order; construct inverses of one-to-one functions; use the identity mapping.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Quadratic representations
nodes.summary: Quadratic representations Move among expanded, factorized and vertex forms; interpret each represen- tation geometrically.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Quadratic equations and inequalities
nodes.summary: Quadratic equations and inequalities Find roots and solution intervals; use the discriminant to determine root counts and parameter restrictions.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Reciprocal and linear rational graphs
nodes.summary: Reciprocal and linear rational graphs Recognize reciprocal structure, excluded inputs, asymptotes and the range of a linear-over-linear function.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Exponential and logarithmic models
nodes.summary: Exponential and logarithmic models Interpret exponential growth and decay, logarithmic graphs, inverse relation- ships and asymptotes.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Analytic and numerical equations
nodes.summary: Analytic and numerical equations Solve equations by algebra or graphing technology; interpret numerical solu- tions in a model.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Basic graph transformations
nodes.summary: Basic graph transformations Combine translations, reflections and horizontal or vertical stretches, respect- ing their order.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Polynomial structure
nodes.summary: Polynomial structure Relate roots, factors and graphs; apply remainder and factor tests; obtain root sums and products.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Further rational functions
nodes.summary: Further rational functions Analyze linear-over-quadratic and quadratic-over-linear expressions, including oblique asymptotes and cancellation.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Symmetry and restricted inverses
nodes.summary: Symmetry and restricted inverses Use odd, even and periodic behavior; restrict a domain for inversion; recognize self-inverse mappings.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Comparing functions
nodes.summary: Comparing functions Solve polynomial and other inequalities by sign analysis or graph intersections.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Further transformations and modulus
nodes.summary: Further transformations and modulus Interpret absolute values of inputs or outputs, reciprocal and squared outputs, and aﬀine input changes; solve modulus conditions.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Coordinates and solids
nodes.summary: Coordinates and solids Find spatial distances and midpoints; work with volumes, exposed surface areas, and right triangles inside solids, including line-plane angles.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: T riangle calculations
nodes.summary: T riangle calculations Choose a right-triangle ratio, sine rule, cosine rule, or sine-area formula to recover a missing measurement.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Navigation and sight lines
nodes.summary: Navigation and sight lines Translate bearings, elevation, and depression into labelled geometric relation- ships and calculate lengths or directions.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Radians and sectors
nodes.summary: Radians and sectors Convert angle units and connect a circle’s radius, central angle, arc length, and sector area.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Unit circle and ambiguous triangles
nodes.summary: Unit circle and ambiguous triangles Use exact circular values and quadrant signs; identify when sine-rule informa- tion permits two different triangles.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Basic trigonometric identities
nodes.summary: Basic trigonometric identities Connect sine, cosine, and tangent using the unit-circle identity and the sine and cosine double-angle formulas.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Trigonometric graphs and models
nodes.summary: Trigonometric graphs and models Read and build sine, cosine, and tangent models using period, amplitude where applicable, shifts, and context.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Trigonometric equations
nodes.summary: Trigonometric equations Find every root in a stated interval, including equations requiring factorization or a quadratic substitution.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Reciprocal and inverse trigonometry
nodes.summary: Reciprocal and inverse trigonometry Use secant, cosecant, and cotangent identities; interpret inverse-trigonometric graphs, domains, ranges, and principal values.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Angle addition
nodes.summary: Angle addition Combine or split angles with sine, cosine, and tangent formulas, including the tangent double-angle formula.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Trigonometric symmetry
nodes.summary: Trigonometric symmetry Use reflection, parity, and periodicity to relate circular functions evaluated at different angles.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: V ector representation and reasoning
nodes.summary: V ector representation and reasoning Use components, magnitudes, unit vectors, scalar multiples, positions, and displacements; complete geometric arguments with vectors.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Scalar products
nodes.summary: Scalar products Calculate angles and test perpendicularity or parallelism through the dot prod- uct and its algebraic properties.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Lines and motion
nodes.summary: Lines and motion Convert vector, parametric, and Cartesian line descriptions; use direction vec- tors for line angles and constant-velocity motion.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Relationships between lines
nodes.summary: Relationships between lines Distinguish identical, parallel, intersecting, and skew lines, checking every co- ordinate when solving for intersections.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: V ector products and area
nodes.summary: V ector products and area Compute oriented cross products; use their properties to find normals and triangle or parallelogram areas.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Plane equations
nodes.summary: Plane equations Represent a plane by a point and two directions, by a normal, or by a Cartesian equation.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Intersections and spatial angles
nodes.summary: Intersections and spatial angles Solve line-plane and plane-system intersections; distinguish geometric out- comes and calculate line-plane or plane-plane angles.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Data quality and sampling
nodes.summary: Data quality and sampling Distinguish populations and samples, discrete and continuous variables; eval- uate bias, missing data, recording errors, outliers and random, convenience, systematic, quota or stratified sampling.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Statistical displays
nodes.summary: Statistical displays Read frequency tables, equal-width histograms, cumulative frequencies and box plots; obtain percentiles and compare distributions using symmetry, me- dians, quartiles, range and IQR.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Location and spread
nodes.summary: Location and spread Calculate mean, median, mode, modal class, variance and standard devi- ation; estimate grouped means; specify quartile conventions and interpret transformed data.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Correlation and predicting y
nodes.summary: Correlation and predicting y Read scatter patterns; use Pearson correlation and the regression of y on x; distinguish association from causation and interpolation from extrapolation.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Probability foundations
nodes.summary: Probability foundations Count outcomes, use relative frequencies and complements, and calculate the expected number of occurrences.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Combining events
nodes.summary: Combining events Use Venn or tree reasoning and outcome tables; handle union, intersection, exclusivity, independence and sampling with or without replacement.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Discrete distributions and expectation
nodes.summary: Discrete distributions and expectation Normalize a probability distribution; calculate expected values and interpret fair prices for games.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Binomial models
nodes.summary: Binomial models Recognize a fixed number of independent fixed-probability trials; calculate individual and cumulative probabilities, means and variances.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Normal models with known parameters
nodes.summary: Normal models with known parameters Use symmetry, probability areas and inverse-normal calculations for a given mean and standard deviation.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Predicting x from y
nodes.summary: Predicting x from y Use the regression of x on y for the appropriate direction of prediction; distin- guish it from rearranging a y-on-x regression.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Conditional probability and independence
nodes.summary: Conditional probability and independence Apply conditional probability algebra; test independence and distinguish it from mutual exclusivity.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Standardization and unknown parameters
nodes.summary: Standardization and unknown parameters Convert between observations and z-scores; recover a normal mean or standard deviation from percentile information.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Bayesian updating
nodes.summary: Bayesian updating Reverse a conditional probability using a partition into at most three cases and the total-probability denominator.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Moments and continuous distributions
nodes.summary: Moments and continuous distributions Use discrete and continuous moments, density normalization, piecewise den- sities, medians and modes; calculate variance and the effect of aﬀine transfor- mations.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Limits and the meaning of a derivative
nodes.summary: Limits and the meaning of a derivative Estimate limits numerically or graphically; interpret a derivative as a tangent gradient or an instantaneous rate.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Increasing and decreasing behaviour
nodes.summary: Increasing and decreasing behaviour Use the sign of the first derivative to locate intervals of increase and decrease.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Differentiating integer powers
nodes.summary: Differentiating integer powers Apply the power rule to integer powers, including negative powers, and to sums of such terms.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: T angents and normals
nodes.summary: T angents and normals Find tangent and normal gradients, equations and intercepts at specified points.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Antiderivatives and numerical integrals
nodes.summary: Antiderivatives and numerical integrals Recover a function from its derivative and a condition; evaluate definite inte- grals and positive areas with technology.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Differentiation rules
nodes.summary: Differentiation rules Differentiate rational powers, sine, cosine, exponential and logarithmic func- tions; apply chain, product and quotient rules.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Second derivatives and graphs
nodes.summary: Second derivatives and graphs Connect a function, its gradient and its curvature; interpret the signs of first and second derivatives.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Extrema, inflexions and optimization
nodes.summary: Extrema, inflexions and optimization Classify stationary points, check changes of concavity and optimize quantities in context.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Motion in one dimension
nodes.summary: Motion in one dimension Connect displacement, velocity, speed and acceleration; distinguish signed dis- placement from total distance.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Standard integrals and reverse chain rule
nodes.summary: Standard integrals and reverse chain rule Integrate powers, trigonometric, exponential and reciprocal expressions; use linear substitutions and recognizable inner derivatives.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Definite integrals and enclosed areas
nodes.summary: Definite integrals and enclosed areas Evaluate integrals exactly or numerically; split signed regions and calculate areas between curves.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: First principles and higher derivatives
nodes.summary: First principles and higher derivatives Understand continuity and differentiability informally; recognize convergent or divergent limits; differentiate polynomials from first principles and calculate higher derivatives.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Indeterminate limits
nodes.summary: Indeterminate limits Resolve zero-over-zero and infinity-over-infinity limits using l’Hopital’s rule, repeated differentiation or Maclaurin expansions.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Implicit differentiation and related rates
nodes.summary: Implicit differentiation and related rates Differentiate implicit relations, connect changing quantities and optimize on restricted domains, including endpoint optima.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Further derivative and integral families
nodes.summary: Further derivative and integral families Use tangent, secant, cosecant, cotangent, general-base exponentials and loga- rithms, and inverse trigonometric functions; integrate using partial fractions.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Substitution and integration by parts
nodes.summary: Substitution and integration by parts Transform integrals with supplied non-obvious substitutions; apply integration by parts once or repeatedly.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Areas with respect to y and solid volumes
nodes.summary: Areas with respect to y and solid volumes Integrate horizontal widths; calculate volumes formed by revolving regions about either coordinate axis.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: First-order differential equations
nodes.summary: First-order differential equations Use Euler steps, separate variables, substitute y=vx in homogeneous equations, or apply an integrating factor; impose initial conditions.

nodes.subject: math
nodes.title: Maclaurin expansions
nodes.summary: Maclaurin expansions Expand exponential, trigonometric, inverse-trigonometric, logarithmic and bi- nomial expressions; obtain further series by substitution, products, calculus or differential equations.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Kinematics
nodes.summary: Kinematics Position, distance and displacement; instantaneous and average motion; gradients and graph areas; constant and changing acceler- ation; projectiles in two dimensions; qualitative fluid resistance.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Forces and momentum
nodes.summary: HL guidance includes two-dimensional collisions.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Work, energy and power
nodes.summary: Work, energy and power Work and energy transfers; kinetic, gravitational and elastic en- ergy; conservation and dissipation; power, eﬀiciency, Sankey dia- grams and fuel energy density.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Rigid body mechanics
nodes.summary: Rigid body mechanics Torque and equilibrium; angular kinematics; inertia and rotation- al dynamics; angular momentum and impulse; rotational energy; coupled bodies and rolling without slipping.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Galilean and special relativity
nodes.summary: Galilean and special relativity Inertial frames; Galilean and Lorentz transformations; light-speed invariance; velocity addition; intervals, proper measurements and simultaneity; spacetime diagrams and muon evidence.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Thermal energy transfers
nodes.summary: Thermal energy transfers Particle descriptions of matter; density and temperature; internal energy; heating and phase changes; conduction, convection and radiation; stellar brightness and thermal spectra.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Greenhouse effect
nodes.summary: Greenhouse effect Reflectivity and emission; intercepted sunlight; molecular infrared absorption; surface and atmosphere energy budgets; equilibrium temperature and changes to the greenhouse effect.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Gas laws
nodes.summary: Gas laws Pressure and particle number; ideal-gas assumptions; state changes; microscopic pressure and rms speed; temperature and molecular energy; monatomic internal energy and model limits.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Thermodynamics
nodes.summary: Thermodynamics First-law signs and work; closed and isolated systems; entropy and microstates; reversible and irreversible processes; gas paths and heat-engine cycles; the Carnot eﬀiciency limit.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Current and circuits
nodes.summary: Current and circuits Charge flow and energy transfer; resistance, resistivity and power; circuit combinations; emf and internal resistance; meters, sources, non-ohmic components and variable-resistance dividers.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Simple harmonic motion
nodes.summary: Model springs and small-angle pendulums; in- terpret energy changes. At AHL, use phase, displacement and ve- locity equations to reconstruct motion and calculate energy quan- titatively.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Wave model
nodes.summary: Distin- guish transverse and longitudinal waves, sound, mechanical and electromagnetic waves, and locate radiation with in the electromag- netic spectrum.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Wave phenomena
nodes.summary: Apply superpo- sition, coherence and Young fringes. At AHL, analyse single-slit envelopes, missing orders and diffraction gratings.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Standing waves and resonance
nodes.summary: Use fixed, free, open and closed bound- aries to calculate permitted harmonics. Interpret resonance, its ap- plications and hazards, and the effects of light, critical and heavy damping.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Doppler effect
nodes.summary: Es- timate slow radial motion from light-frequency or wavelength changes. At AHL, calculate sound shifts and infer speeds for a moving source or a moving observer, considered separately.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Gravitational fields
nodes.summary: At AHL, connect potential gradients, equipotential surfaces and work; calculate escape and circular-orbit speeds, satellite energy changes and the qualitative effects of atmospheric drag.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Electric and magnetic fields
nodes.summary: At AHL, combine scalar potentials and relate potential gradients, equipotentials, work and interac- tion energy.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Motion in electromagnetic fields
nodes.summary: Apply magnetic forces to charges and current-carrying wires, determine charge-to-mass ratios, analyse velocity selectors and curved trajectories, and calculate interactions between parallel currents.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Induction
nodes.summary: Analyse moving rods, translating rectangular coils and rotating generators, includ- ing rotation-frequency effects and qualitative self-induction.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Structure of the atom
nodes.summary: Structure of the atom Use scattering and spectra to test atomic models; count nucleons; calculate transitions, nuclear sizes, closest approach and quantized hydrogen orbits.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Quantum physics
nodes.summary: Quantum physics Link photoelectric data to photons; use matter-wave diffraction, de Broglie momentum and Compton scattering with energy con- servation.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Radioactive decay
nodes.summary: Radioactive decay Balance nuclear changes; interpret binding and radiation evidence; model counts, backgrounds, populations, activity, half-life, decay probabilities and applications.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Fission
nodes.summary: Fission Balance fission reactions; calculate released energy and chain be- haviour; connect reactor components, fuel use, eﬀiciency and radioactive-product management.

nodes.subject: physics
nodes.title: Fusion and stars
nodes.summary: Fusion and stars Relate fusion and pressure support to stellar evolution; interpret HR regions and spectra; infer distance, luminosity and radius with uncertainties.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
nodes.summary: Connect temperature with particle motion, use state symbols, and analyse practical evidence from heating, cooling, sol- ubility and more than one chromatography method.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: The nuclear atom
nodes.summary: Use isotope proportions to ex- plain average atomic masses and reconstruct unknown composi- tions. At HL, extract isotope identities and abundances from mass spectra, combining graphical evidence with particle and mixture accounting.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Electron configurations
nodes.summary: Interpret orbital occupancy and the chromium and copper exceptions. HL work adds ionization trends, spectral convergence calculations, and deductions from successive ionization energies.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Counting particles by mass: The mole
nodes.summary: Deter- mine empirical and molecular formulas from analytical data, plan solution preparation and dilution, and connect gaseous volume ra- tios with balanced reactions under matched conditions.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Ideal gases
nodes.summary: Interpret graphs, infer molar masses and analyse changing gas samples using consistent units. Evaluate when real gases depart from the model and propagate measurement uncertainty in experimental gas calculations.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: The ionic model
nodes.summary: Use lattice structure, mobile charge carriers, ion size and charge to reason about melting, conductivity, solubility and relative lattice strength.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: The covalent model
nodes.summary: Extend bonding models through resonance, benzene evidence, expanded valence shells, formal charge, orbital overlap and hybridization to interpret both organic and inorganic species.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: The metallic model
nodes.summary: Com- pare bonding trends using charge, size and electron density, eval- uate simple models against data, and consider the contribution of transition metals’ d-electrons.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: From models to materials
nodes.summary: Infer addition monomers and repeat units, then analyse polyester and polyamide formation, hydrolysis, terminal groups and the loss of small molecules.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: The periodic table: Classification of elements
nodes.summary: Examine ionization-energy exceptions and transition- element chemistry through ion configurations, characteristic prop- erties and the relationship between absorbed light, observed colour and energy.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Functional groups: Classification of organic compounds
nodes.summary: Analyse stereoisomerism and opti- cal behaviour, then combine mass fragments, infrared bands and proton NMR signals, integration and splitting to identify compact organic structures.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Measuring enthalpy changes
nodes.summary: Use temperature measurements to determine enthalpy changes, ac- counting for reacting amounts, calorimeter heat capacity, heat loss and the limitations of experimental assumptions.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Energy cycles in reactions
nodes.summary: Use formation and combustion data with the ap- propriate stoichiometric factors, distinguish standard states, and interpret Born–Haber cycles involving singly or doubly charged ions and explicit lattice-enthalpy conventions.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Energy from fuels
nodes.summary: Interpret hydrogen and methanol fuel- cell electrode equations, connecting electron balance with fuel use, oxygen demand and reaction products.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Entropy and spontaneity
nodes.summary: Combine enthalpy, entropy and temperature to evaluate Gibbs energy and feasibility; distinguish thermodynamic direc- tion from reaction speed. Connect non-standard composition, re- action quotient and equilibrium constants, including inverse and temperature-threshold problems.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: How much? The amount of chemical change
nodes.summary: Identify limiting and excess reagents, distinguish actual from theoretical yields, and compare atom e- conomy with yield. Solve inverse composition, purity, sequential processing and residual-mixture problems using conserved atoms.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: How fast? The rate of chemical change
nodes.summary: Interpret multistep mechanisms and energy profiles; infer rate laws, reaction orders and rate-constant units from evidence, and extract activation energy and frequency factors from Arrhe- nius data.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: How far? The extent of chemical change
nodes.summary: Use concentration expressions, reaction quotients and Gibbs energy to predict direction and determine composition. Solve inverse equi- librium problems, apply justified small-conversion approximations and track conserved reacting amounts.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Proton transfer reactions
nodes.summary: Ex- tend to weak-acid and weak-base equilibria, salt hydrolysis, in- dicators, titration curves and buffers, including the assumptions behind quantitative pH calculations.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Electron transfer reactions
nodes.summary: At HL, compare electrode potentials, connect cell potential to Gibbs energy, and predict aqueous electrolysis and electroplating behaviour.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Electron sharing reactions
nodes.summary: Track regenerated radicals, infer net reactions and product mixtures, and connect molecular symmetry, experimental conditions and sup- plied quantitative models to reaction outcomes.

nodes.subject: chemistry
nodes.title: Electron-pair sharing reactions
nodes.summary: At HL, use Lewis acid-base and coordination models, compare SN1 and SN2 mechanisms and stereochemistry, and explain carbocation-controlled addition and electrophilic substitution of benzene.

edges.note: Both develop differentiation from first principles.
SHM uses kinematics of oscillating displacement.
Periodic trends follow from electron configurations.
